clue.text: Check about object, present for turning over in ongoing dispute

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another
turning a thing over flips it end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
an end is an aim or object
present at a meeting is at it

explanation.surface: Someone checks over a gift that has been flipped over in the middle of a long quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it means being in attendance, as in present at a meeting. An end is an object in the sense of an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, often between families, so it is a quarrel that keeps going.

clue.text: Revelations, etc. not apparent in present, perhaps in future

definitions.text: not apparent in present, perhaps in future

blocks.note: Revelation and its neighbours are the late books of the Bible
those books belong to the New Testament, NT

explanation.surface: Biblical prophecies whose meaning is hidden now but may become clear in times to come.
explanation.walkthrough: Revelation closes the Bible, so it and the books near it are the late New Testament: LATE + NT. The definition fits the puzzle's theme of tenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent exists already but lies dormant and hidden, possibly emerging or developing later on.

clue.text: Cook focuses, eclipsing husband who’s inferior in kitchen?

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or falsify it, so the letters are rearranged
to eclipse something is to block it from view by covering it, so one piece hides inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A cook concentrating on the stove while a husband plays second fiddle in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the rearranged letters wrap round H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sous-chef is the second in command of a professional kitchen, ranking below the head chef.

clue.text: Scientific genius of past or present century

blocks.note: what is present or current is new
a ton is a hundred, as a century is

explanation.surface: Asking whether a great scientist belongs to history or to our own times.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'past or present' as a pair, but 'present century' is the wordplay. TON is slang for a hundred, so a century.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton, the seventeenth-century physicist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity, is a famous historical scientist.

clue.text: Keep changing position as witness, and did so previously

blocks.note: to witness is to see
saw is the past of see, what a witness did before

explanation.surface: A wavering witness whose story keeps shifting, and who wavered before too.
explanation.walkthrough: The present and past of the same verb sit side by side, in keeping with the puzzle's theme of tenses.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to swing repeatedly back and forth between two states, like a teeter-totter rising and falling.

clue.text: Polish a large kind of shoe

blocks.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone buffs up a big shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the lower-case verb disguised by its place at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on with straps, a style of footwear.

clue.text: Not totally anxious, having absorbed reasonable signs

indicators.note: what is not totally there is incomplete, so a letter is dropped
to absorb something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: tense means anxious; its final letter goes
OK means acceptable or reasonable

explanation.surface: A slightly nervous person taking in sensible indications.
explanation.walkthrough: TENSE loses its last letter, then holds OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokens are signs or symbols, as in a token of gratitude, marking or standing for something.

clue.text: Food for winter is laid up with a lot of beer

indicators.note: in a down entry, laid up means set upward, so the letters read bottom to top
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the end is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
lager is a type of beer; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Stocking up winter supplies and keeping plenty of beer in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' sounds like stored away for winter, but in a down entry it sends the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented grass or fodder stored in a silo to feed livestock during the cold months.

clue.text: Will indicates this, in contrast to 13

definitions.text: Will indicates this, in contrast to 13

blocks.note: surface reading: a legal will points to what happens after a death

blocks.clueFragment: Will indicates this, in contrast to 13
blocks.note: setter's reading: the auxiliary verb 'will' marks the grammatical time to come, the opposite of the earlier tense at 13

explanation.surface: Someone's will spells out what will happen, unlike a backward-looking entry elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is capitalised as the first word, so it reads as a testament, but it is the grammar word. Entry 13 is PAST PERFECT, a backward-looking tense.
explanation.definitionFit: In English grammar the auxiliary 'will' forms the verb tense describing events still to come.

clue.text: Stationed at border, feeling nervous

blocks.note: first meaning: literally placed on the rim
second meaning: jumpy, tense

explanation.surface: A border guard posted at the frontier is understandably jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes one sentence of a nervous sentry, but the two halves are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally positioned at a rim and, idiomatically, irritable or anxious.

clue.text: You reportedly get irritated about son, or get worried

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the letter U sounds like the word you
to nettle is to irritate or annoy
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent is annoyed with their son, or else frets about him.
explanation.walkthrough: The nettle plant stings, which is why its name became a verb for irritating someone. The definition is transitive: to unsettle is to get someone worried.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to make them anxious or disturbed, getting them into a worried state.

clue.text: Stressed being educated soundly

indicators.note: done soundly means by sound, so the spoken form is wanted rather than the spelling

blocks.note: one who has been educated has been taught

explanation.surface: Someone who is thoroughly schooled but under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', modifying educated, but it signals a sound-alike. In non-rhotic speech the two words are identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut describes something pulled tight under tension, as a stressed rope or nerve is.

clue.text: Engage in an emotional farewell? It’s cliffhanging

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: be touched, then leave
second meaning: precariously uncertain

explanation.surface: A tearful goodbye that leaves everyone in suspense.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical first reading: an emotional parting is one where you are touched and then you go.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation whose outcome is highly uncertain and risky until the very end.

clue.text: Statement of unrealistic nostalgia that makes one tense

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the claim that bygone days were flawless
second meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'had gone'

explanation.surface: Rose-tinted longing for the good old days makes a person uptight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for a person but is the grammar noun. The first half is a whole sentence squeezed into two words: the past was perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: The pluperfect, formed with 'had' plus a participle, describes action completed before another earlier moment.

clue.text: Speculations in article on products of mine one’s invested in

indicators.note: money invested in a venture is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the definite article
ores are what a mine produces
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Guesswork in a newspaper piece about the output of a mine somebody has a stake in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive but is the pit. In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the article comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are proposed explanations or conjectures not yet proven, much like guesses or hypotheses.

clue.text: Uses a name time after time – in past, present, and future

blocks.note: to con is to exploit or use someone by trickery
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a name over and over in every period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' looks like 'repeatedly'; it is T placed after A-N-T's opening T: A, N and T come after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant is unchanging and permanent, existing the same way at every moment through all of time.

clue.text: Need for drink after second shift in t-shirt

indicators.note: shifting the second letter moves it out of its place, so the order changes

blocks.note: taken as written, the hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Someone wants a drink after a second work shift spent in a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second shift' sounds like a work period; move the second letter, S, of TSHIRT along three places.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is the bodily craving for liquid, the desire felt when the body needs water.

clue.text: Beat rivals, then beat rivals up – that’s separate

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to beat rivals is to win
the past form: having beaten them, you won

explanation.surface: A sporting boast: beat the opposition, then beat them again.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase gives present then past, WIN then WON, matching the tense theme; the second is turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow is to sift grain from chaff by blowing air through it, so to sort apart.

clue.text: Incomparable time spent there, agitated

indicators.note: something agitated is shaken up, so its letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wonderful holiday spent somewhere, recalled with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomparable time' alludes to the saying 'there's no time like the present'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says no moment matches now for acting, so the current moment is the one beyond comparison.

clue.text: Arrange flags around an old-fashioned dance

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to pave is to lay flagstones
taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorating with bunting for a period dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' suggests bunting but means flagstones, the paving slabs laid on a path.
explanation.definitionFit: The pavane is a slow, stately processional court dance popular in sixteenth-century Europe.

clue.text: Bans that are initially followed by audible disapproval

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the start, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
boos are noisy jeers of disapproval

explanation.surface: Prohibitions that are greeted at first by jeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible disapproval' is not a sound-alike signal here; it simply describes the jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboos are social or religious prohibitions forbidding certain acts, words or customs.

clue.text: Some quick coverage that is hammered home

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the hard plate covering the quick of a finger
second meaning: a metal spike driven in by a hammer

explanation.surface: Brief news reporting that drives a point home forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as fast, but the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingernail shields the sensitive skin beneath it, and a carpenter's metal pin is driven in with blows.

clue.text: Religious text supporting parts of speech

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
verbs are one class of word, a part of speech

explanation.surface: Scripture backing up passages of a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of speech' suggests extracts from an address, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of wise sayings attributed to Solomon.

clue.text: Cruel grown-up hiding food container

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside out of view, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a grown-up child is big
a tin holds food

explanation.surface: A heartless adult secretly keeping a lunchbox to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grown-up' wants to be a noun for an adult; here it is an adjective meaning large.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting remarks or winds are harsh and wounding, so the word suits something unkind and sharp.

clue.text: Became uneasy in end and set off

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled or gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone grew nervous at the finish and then departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as departed, but 'off' alone is the signal acting on both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tensed is to have grown taut and nervous, physically or emotionally stiffening with anxiety.

clue.text: Chinese food has to be divided and returned in future, perhaps

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a wonton is a Chinese dumpling

explanation.surface: A Chinese dish must be shared out and sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Divided into two words and written backwards, the dumpling becomes a two-word phrase of postponement.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something should happen later rather than at this moment puts it off, possibly till another day.
